finding_id: - Description: Attackers can exploit the login system by inserting malicious SQL commands into the login fields. This may allow them to access administrator accounts without knowing the correct username or password
title: giving them control over application data and administrative functions.

finding_id: - Recommendation: Use prepared statements or parameterized queries when handling login credentials. This ensures that user input is treated as data instead of executable SQL commands.
JUICE-002.png – SQL Injection (Data Extraction via Search)
- Description: Attackers can manipulate the product search function using SQL injection to access information stored in the database. This could expose sensitive user details
title: including email addresses

finding_id: - Recommendation: Apply parameterized queries to product searches and validate user input to prevent malicious SQL commands from being executed.
- Description: Attackers can insert malicious JavaScript into the search parameter
title: causing the script to run in another user's browser. This could put user sessions at risk
url_or_endpoint: or redirect users to harmful websites.

finding_id: - Recommendation: Properly encode user input before displaying it on webpages. Implement a Content Security Policy (CSP) to help prevent unauthorized scripts from executing.
- Description: Attackers can save malicious JavaScript through input fields
title: such as feedback forms. The script may automatically execute whenever an administrator or another user views the saved content
vuln_type: potentially compromising their account and allowing unauthorized actions.

finding_id: - Recommendation: Sanitize user-submitted content using trusted libraries like DOMPurify. Also
title: apply HTML entity encoding when displaying saved information to prevent malicious scripts from executing.
